rv.q: Malloy’s music is, after all, intoxicating. Alcohol is the accelerant for the show’s linked monodramas. And hung over is how it leaves its pandemic-sozzled characters at the end of a dark karaoke night of the soul.
Malloy produces lovely passages, but dramatic tension and character development is where Three Houses starts to wobble on its foundations.
It might be satisfying, in a 'clicking in your head' way, to construct a work so that all the elements line up, but it's less satisfying to watch.
Malloy's gamble with tone, format, approach, and subject matter more than pays off.
I was simply thrilled to see a writer shoot for the moon and pretty much get there.
Run, don't walk, to dive into a new Dave Malloy musical, Three Houses
